chunks: And as for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad, all of them from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār from Abū Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the sacrificial animal (hady), whether something from it is taken out of the Sanctuary (Haram). He said: 'The skin, the hump, and whatever is beneficial.' I said: 'It has reached us from your father that he said: "Nothing from the guaranteed sacrificial animal is taken out."' He said: 'Rather, that which is beneficial is taken out.' And Aḥmad added: 'And nothing of the meat is taken out of the Haram.'

And this does not contradict what we mentioned, because in the report there is not a general permission of that in all cases, and it is permissible that he (peace be upon him) only permitted it for the one who gives its price in charity. And that which indicates this is what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: Can parts of the Hajj sacrificial animal be taken out of the Haram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between reports by distinguishing between the general prohibition of removing meat and the specific permissibility of exporting the skin, hump, and other utilitarian parts. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that exceptions to ritual restrictions are often contextual, such as allowing the export of beneficial items when their value is donated, thereby reconciling textual evidence with practical application.
